newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Wednesday.

"Government securities were narrowly mixed on continued uncertainty over the near-term direction of the market. Treasury bill yields were narrowly mixed but bond prices were slightly higher. The interbank rate was unchanged and volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.22/2.17 percent compared with Tuesday's yield of 2.13/2.08 percent.
One-year closed at a yield of 2.42/2.37 percent against 2.43/2.38 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.03/98.08 from Tuesday's close of S$97.95/98.00, September 2001 at S$97.13/97.18 versus S$96.95/97.00 and June 2003 at S$95.15/95.20 against S$94.92/94.97.
The overnight interbank offered rate was unchanged from Tuesday's 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent.
